title: The README changes only as its Surface item says

statements.says: The README Surface, found by its heading "## The README", is the one route by which the loop changes the README.
A spec names the README only in its Surfaces section.
The spec review removes any README edit its README item does not ask for.
How much a README item may ask for is the Surface's "What to capture", which the team owns.
The Seed allows a line that changes and one new item in the setup or run steps, and never a new sentence or section.
The drift check reads the README on every spec, and a link, path or command the spec broke is a Gap.
A change that deserves new README text goes into the spec's Out of Scope as a focused session, and nothing builds it.
A repo with no README Surface gets none of these README rules.
The Plugin fixes that the README item is the only route by which the loop changes the README.
That the README item is the only route is method, and the Plugin fixes method.
The loop grew the README one ticket at a time, each spec and builder adding a sentence, until the page was a long reference nobody read to the end.
Most of the commits that grew the README came from tickets, although the README was never one of the repo's Surfaces.
A README is a pitch and a way in, and only a focused session writes one well.
The drift check reading the README means a rename the grill missed is still caught.
How much the loop may write in a README is taste, and a team steers its taste.
Removing the README Surface was rejected, because the appending never came from the Surface and without it nothing would catch a rename that left the README naming something gone.
Having the landing refuse a ticket that changes the README was rejected, because a script cannot tell a rename from a new paragraph and the Gap and rename tickets have to touch the README.
Having the loop never touch the README was rejected, because the README would be wrong between focused sessions and a wrong setup step is the worst error a README can hold.
Having the Plugin fix the limit on README changes was rejected, because how much the loop may write in a README is taste, which a team steers.
